Subject: Trial grant accounting treatment & invoice offset — VerdantHealth

Hi Marissa —

VerdantHealth (deal DH-98422) is asking for an additional trial grant: $12,000 in credits plus a 30-day extension. Customer asked our AE to either have the amount posted as an invoice offset to their outstanding invoice (INV-5538) or to issue a credit memo — they prefer the simplest path that won’t delay their PO/close.

Quick context: Verdant signed a 6-month pilot in March and we invoiced their first month on 4/1 (INV-5538). They’ve used ~60% of the trial allotment. At request of the AE, we offered a one-time grant to cover extra usage from a spike during POC. Sales captured the signed trial amendment (attached).

Questions for finance:
- For audit and month-end, do you prefer we issue a formal credit memo tied to INV-5538, or can we apply a negative invoice (invoice offset) to the outstanding receivable?
- Any preferred GLA for this type of one-off trial grant? (I recall contra-revenue vs discount handling difference)
- Will applying an offset now create any revenue recognition adjustment we need to flag? Fiscal month-end is 4/30.

Attachments: Verdant_trial_agreement.pdf, Verdant_PO_4521.pdf

Action: Can you confirm routing and ETA today? Verdant needs confirmation to proceed with their billing team.

Thanks —
Monica
Monica Patel
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
monica@redwoodinference.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2027-04-07T12:24:00Z
Subject: Re: Trial grant accounting treatment & invoice offset — VerdantHealth

Thanks Monica — quick questions before I route to Accounting:

1) Was any of the $12k already recognized as revenue? (i.e., did we recognize full ARR for any portion of the pilot?)
2) Please confirm the invoice number to which the offset would be applied (you mentioned INV-5538).
3) Do we have a signed amendment or PO that references the grant amount (send if available).

Initial guidance: normally we issue a credit memo referencing the original invoice so there’s a clear audit trail. Contra-revenue classification is typical for promotional grants, but I’ll confirm the exact GLA mapping with Marcus. If revenue for the invoiced period has already been recognized, we may need an RRA (revenue reversal adjustment).

I’m attaching a GLA_mapping_template.xlsx — Marcus, can you advise GLA and whether this should be contra-revenue or a deduction from AR? Also need to confirm if this is a reduction of gross revenue or a separate marketing expense.

If we can get the signed amendment and PO (attached), I’ll draft the credit memo and target issuance by 4/09 EOD if accounting confirms.

—Marissa

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2027-04-08T09:15:00Z
Subject: Re: Trial grant accounting treatment & invoice offset — VerdantHealth

Quick note from Accounting: classify as a customer rebate (contra-revenue) under GLA 5401. Rationale: it reduces gross revenue attributable to the billed period and preserves the receivable/cash movement audit trail when tied to an invoice.

Proposed journal entries if we issue a credit memo tied to INV-5538: 
- Debit: Revenue Contra (GLA 5401) — $12,000
- Credit: Accounts Receivable (INV-5538) — $12,000

If revenue was already recognized for the period, we will also process an RRA to adjust recognized revenue on the income statement. Please flag if Verdant’s PO corresponds to revenue we recognized.

Marcus

All — thanks for the quick turnaround. I’ve drafted a credit memo (credit_memo_draft.pdf) referencing INV-5538 and coded it to GLA 5401. Action items: 

1) Monica: please confirm in this thread that Verdant accepts a credit memo and that the contacts on the PO are correct. If Asha confirms now, I’ll publish the credit memo and post the AR adjustment tomorrow morning (4/10) before EOD close.
2) Marcus/Accounting: please prepare the RRA if we determine revenue was recognized for the invoiced period — I’ll flag if needed after posting.
3) Neha: please confirm whether the credit memo needs to hit a specific customer sub-ledger mapping for Verdant.

Asha — please confirm acceptance so we can close this out quickly and keep the customer happy.

Thanks —
Marissa
